# Eläinklinikka Saari — full site text (English)

> Eläinklinikka Saari is a family-owned small-animal veterinary clinic in Vaasa, Finland, operating since 1989. It cares for dogs, cats and small mammals, as well as exotic species and wildlife, and offers dentistry, surgery (orthopedic, soft-tissue), cardiology, ultrasound, endoscopy, vaccinations, laboratory and imaging (X-ray, ultrasound). Service is available in Finnish, Swedish and English. Address: Gerbyntie 18, 65230 Vaasa. Phone: +358 6 321 7300. Open Monday–Friday 07:45–17:00.

### About the Clinic

Vaasa's only family-owned independent small animal clinic – since 1989
For us, patient welfare and client satisfaction are our top priorities. We strive to create a warm and trusting relationship with both you and your pet.
Our professional care team offers experienced and knowledgeable service, always in the best interest of your pet. During opening hours we also reserve slots for urgent cases — see emergency instructions.
Comprehensive Diagnostics
X-ray, ultrasound, endoscopy, laboratory
Modern Surgery
Orthopedics and soft tissue surgery
Cardiac Examinations
Official cardiac ultrasound examinations
Extensive Dental Care
Dental X-rays, extractions and complicated cases

### Our Services

We offer comprehensive veterinary services for your pet

#### Emergency

Daily reserved acute slots weekdays 7:45–17. Evenings and weekends: regional hotline 0600 399 299. First aid guidance for emergencies.

#### Acupuncture

Acupuncture is used for pain relief and for the treatment of some diseases. Administered by Assaf, who has completed further training in canine and equine acupuncture.

#### Blood Tests

Most samples are examined in our own laboratory, so you can get results during the same visit.

#### Dermatology & Allergies

Skin diseases are one of the most common reasons to seek veterinary care. About one in ten dogs in Finland has allergies, which often cause skin and ear infections. Typical symptoms include paw licking, ear scratching, and face rubbing. When allergy is suspected, we first try to rule out food as a cause, and if necessary, collect allergy blood samples.

#### Pregnancy Diagnosis

Ultrasound can confirm pregnancy from approximately day 24. X-ray examination can provide a more accurate estimate of the number of puppies from approximately day 50.

#### Endoscopy

We perform video-otoscopy (ear canal examination and flushing), rhinoscopy (nasal cavity examination), gastroscopy (gastrointestinal examination), cystoscopy (urinary tract examination) and bronchoscopy (airway examination).

#### Therapeutic Diets

We carry special therapeutic diets used as part of the treatment for various conditions. Recommended for osteoarthritis, renal failure, gastrointestinal diseases, food allergies, urinary tract diseases, and weight management. Brands: Royal Canin, Specific, Hill's.

#### Wellness & Rehabilitation

Wellness and rehabilitation services to assess and improve your pet's mobility and function. Common reasons include reduced mobility, pain following trauma, and post-surgical recovery. Services: gait analysis, deep massage, electrotherapy, customized training programs.

#### Health Examinations

During health checks we can detect changes that may cause health problems in the long run. The vet performs a full clinical examination, listens to the heart and lungs and, if necessary, takes blood samples.

#### Heart Diseases

Heart diseases are common, especially in certain breeds. Early treatment can extend your pet's lifespan and improve quality of life. We offer cardiac ultrasound, ECG and Holter monitoring. We also perform official heart ultrasound examinations for dogs. We are authorized to perform official heart auscultation examinations.

#### Castration

We castrate cats, dogs and rabbits. Dog castration can prevent prostate problems and urine marking. Chemical castration with a hormonal implant is also available (6 or 12-month duration).

#### Soft Tissue Surgery

Spays, neuters, caesarean sections, tumor removals, foreign body extraction, bladder stone surgery, other abdominal surgeries, and eye and ear procedures.

#### Orthopedic Surgery

The clinic has a dedicated orthopedic surgery room with a higher level of sterility. We have been performing knee surgeries since 2017. Cruciate ligament repair with two methods: lateral suture technique stabilizes the joint with synthetic support material, and TTA (tibial tuberosity advancement) alters knee biomechanics by advancing the tibial tuberosity forward. Also patellar luxation surgery, fracture repairs, amputations and femoral head ostectomy for chronic luxation or Legg-Perthes disease.

#### Laboratory

Well-equipped in-house laboratory: blood samples, urine samples, blood smears, skin and ear samples. Most results available during your visit. Analyses: hematology, clinical chemistry, electrolytes, hormones, urine cultures, cytology.

#### Official Examinations

Official hip, elbow and back X-rays. Official knee examinations. Official heart auscultations. Official heart ultrasound examinations for dogs.

#### X-ray

Digital X-ray. Recommended for limping, respiratory or cardiac symptoms, acute vomiting, urinary problems, tumor suspicion, and official screening X-rays.

#### Final Farewell – Euthanasia

We strive to make the final farewell peaceful and unhurried. Your pet first receives a sedative with pain relief, followed by an anesthetic. Options: home burial, cremation, or individual cremation with urn.

#### Sterilization

A common procedure for dogs, cats and rabbits. Sterilization helps prevent hormonal diseases including mammary tumors and uterine infections. General anesthesia with comprehensive pain management.

#### Dental Care

Dental disorders are very common — by age 3, most dogs and cats have some dental inflammation. Services: tartar removal with ultrasound, dental X-rays, surgical tooth extractions, deciduous teeth removals, and removal of unerupted teeth and cysts. All procedures under general anesthesia with inhalation anesthesia, intravenous fluids and comprehensive pain management.

#### Ultrasound

High-quality ultrasound: abdominal examinations, uterine examinations, liver, kidney and other organ examinations, and heart ultrasound.

#### Vaccinations

Vaccinations are an important part of preventive healthcare. Puppies are usually vaccinated at 12 and 16 weeks of age, kittens likewise. Adults are vaccinated every 1–3 years.

#### Puppy Examinations

The veterinarian examines the puppy thoroughly from head to toe and issues a health certificate. A microchip can be implanted during the visit.

#### Internal Medicine

Internal medicine covers a wide range of animal diseases: diabetes, Cushing's disease, pancreatitis, anaemia, autoimmune diseases. Thorough diagnostics and treatment planning.

#### Ophthalmology

Eye diseases are common in pets. Corneal ulcers, glaucoma, dry eye, cataracts, eyelid diseases. Examination and treatment during the same visit.

#### EU Pet Passport

EU pet passports, rabies vaccination, titre testing and health certificates. All travel documents under one roof.

#### Anesthesia

Anesthesia is close to our hearts. We continuously update our education, refresh our protocols and monitor patients closely throughout every procedure. The clinic has advanced monitoring equipment, four anesthesia machines and two ventilators to ensure safe anesthesia.

#### Hygiene

A high level of hygiene is of utmost importance to us. Examination tables are disinfected between patients and blankets and pads are washed after every use. We use UV light to disinfect clinic areas and filters with inhalation anesthesia. Floors are disinfected twice daily.
Online shop

### Pet food online, collected at the clinic

Order Royal Canin food for your cat or dog online and collect it at our reception. A range chosen by our vets, no fad diets.

### We are a Silver accredited Cat Friendly Clinic

We want to minimise stress for cats visiting our clinic, so we are an International Cat Care Cat Friendly Clinic.
In 2020 we became the first Cat Friendly Clinic in Ostrobothnia, as reported by Yle (in Finnish) and Vasabladet (in Swedish).

#### THIS IS OUR PROMISE TO YOU:

- We are gentle and caring with cats
- We understand the needs of cats
- We have cat friendly facilities
Please ask any of our staff if you would like to see our clinic or if you have any questions.
Cat vet in Vaasa: how we care for cats →
To find out more visit: iCatCare.org
International Cat Care is a charity working towards a world where all cats, owned and unowned, are treated with care, compassion and understanding.

### Wildlife

In cooperation with Nordic Wildlife Care
Animal Clinic Saari cooperates with Nordic Wildlife Care. Our volunteer work is free of charge.
We provide diagnostic and treatment services for injured wild animals. Animals receive initial care before transfer to rehabilitation centers, with the goal of releasing them back into nature.
Support wildlife care by donating to Nordic Wildlife Care
Found an injured wild animal? Contact the rehabilitation facility or bring the animal directly to the clinic.
Read wildlife patient stories →

### Frequently asked questions

#### Where is Eläinklinikka Saari located?

We are at Gerbyntie 18, 65230 Vaasa, in the Dragnäsbäck district at Pukinkulma. We are easy to reach from the surrounding municipalities too.

#### What are Eläinklinikka Saari's opening hours?

The clinic is open Monday to Friday 7:45–17 and closed at weekends. We reserve acute slots every day for urgent cases.

#### Do you have emergency service in the evenings and at weekends?

In the evenings and at weekends, call the Northern emergency-area number 0600 399 299. On weekdays 7:45–17 we have acute slots available daily.

#### Which animals do you treat?

We treat dogs, cats and other small pets such as rabbits and rodents. We are an officially Cat Friendly certified clinic.

#### How do I book an appointment with the vet?

You can book online or by calling (06) 321 7300. No referral is needed.

#### What languages do you serve in?

We serve in Finnish, Swedish and English.

# Services | Saari Animal Clinic

URL: https://elainklinikkasaari.fi/en/services/
Last updated: 2026-10-15

## Our Services

Eläinklinikka Saari offers a comprehensive range of small-animal veterinary services in Vaasa. We have been operating in Dragnäsbäck since 1989, and our team includes six veterinarians and eight veterinary nurses. We serve in English, Finnish and Swedish. Below you'll find all 26 of our services — click any service to learn more.

### Examinations and Check-ups

- Puppy Check-up — puppy and kitten check-up, microchip, vaccination programme and deworming.
- Senior Check-up — senior pet check-up €299 — vet visit, blood sampling and full IDEXX panel in one price.
- Official Examinations — official hip, elbow, patella and cardiac screenings — Finnish Kennel Club approved.

### Vaccinations and Travel

- Vaccinations — puppy vaccination programme, booster shots and rabies.
- EU Pet Passport — EU pet passport, rabies vaccination, titre testing and health certificates.

### Dental Care

- Dental Care — scaling, dental X-rays and extractions. All procedures under general anaesthesia.

### Internal Medicine and Specialty Care

- Internal Medicine — diabetes, Cushing's, pancreatitis and anaemia — diagnostics and treatment.
- Dermatology and Allergies — allergy testing, ear infections and itching — diagnosis and treatment.
- Ophthalmology — corneal ulcers, glaucoma, dry eye and cataracts.

### Surgery and Anaesthesia

- Surgery — soft tissue surgery, orthopaedics, TTA and lateral suture.
- Orthopaedics — cruciate ligament repair (TTA, lateral suture), fracture surgery and amputations.
- Spaying — spaying for female dogs, cats and rabbits under general anaesthesia.
- Castration — castration for male dogs, cats and rabbits, including chemical castration with Suprelorin implant.
- Anaesthesia — inhalation anaesthesia, continuous monitoring and balanced protocol.

### Diagnostics and Imaging

- X-ray — digital X-ray and dental radiography — high-quality images, rapid results.
- Ultrasound — abdominal and cardiac ultrasound plus pregnancy scanning.
- Cardiac Examinations — cardiac ultrasound, ECG and Holter — official breeding screenings.
- Endoscopy — gastroscopy, video otoscopy, rhinoscopy, cystoscopy and bronchoscopy.
- Laboratory — in-house lab: blood tests, urinalysis, cytology and hormones.
- Blood Tests — haematology, clinical chemistry, hormones and urine cultures — results during your visit.
- Pregnancy Examination — ultrasound, X-ray and fetal monitoring — C-section planning.

### Wellness and Rehabilitation

- Acupuncture — pain relief, musculoskeletal conditions and neurological symptoms.
- Rehabilitation — mobility analysis, massage, electrotherapy and post-surgical rehab.
- Food and prescription diets – Royal Canin everyday food online, collected at the clinic. Prescription diets at the clinic only.
- Hygiene — UV disinfection, surface disinfection and ISFM cat-friendly standards.

### Final Farewell

- Final Farewell — Euthanasia — pain-free euthanasia with sedation. Cremation and individual cremation available.
Not sure which service is right for your pet? Give us a call — we'll happily help you choose.

### Frequently asked questions

#### What services does Eläinklinikka Saari offer?

Our services include vaccinations, dental care, surgery (orthopaedic and soft-tissue), cardiac examinations and ultrasound, endoscopy, dermatology, internal medicine, and EU pet passports.

#### Do you perform surgery and dental care?

Yes. We perform both orthopaedic and soft-tissue surgery, and provide dental care with digital dental X-ray.

#### Do you do cardiac examinations and ultrasound?

Yes. We perform cardiac ultrasound examinations, and our clinic has a heart examiner authorised by the Finnish Kennel Club (Leena Sandström).

#### How much does a vet visit cost?

A consultation costs 45 € (under 15 min) or 80 € (under 30 min). Procedures and examinations are priced separately — see the price list.

#### Do I need a referral, or can I book directly?

No referral is needed. You can book directly online or by calling the clinic.

#### Is the clinic cat-friendly?

Yes. We are an officially Cat Friendly certified clinic and accommodate cats' special needs with calm, gentle handling.

# Contact – Saari Animal Clinic, Vaasa

URL: https://elainklinikkasaari.fi/en/contact/
Last updated: 2026-10-15

## Contact

### Address and location

Saari Animal Clinic
Gerbyntie 18
65230 Vaasa
(Dragnäsbäck, at Pukinkulma)

### Directions

By car: The clinic is in the Dragnäsbäck district, at the junction of Gerbyntie and Pohjolankatu (Pukinkulma). It's about a 5-minute drive from Vaasa city centre. Drive south along Wolffintie and turn onto Gerbyntie — the clinic is on the right. Free parking is available in the car park in front of the clinic, with space for several cars.
By bus: The nearest bus stops are on Gerbyntie right outside the clinic, less than 100 metres away. Vaasa local bus line 1 runs along the route. Check timetables at vaasa.fi.

### Phone and email

Phone: (06) 321 7300
Email: info@saarivet.fi
We answer the phone on weekdays during opening hours. For non-urgent matters you can also send an email or a WhatsApp message, and we'll reply as soon as possible.

### Opening hours

Mon–Fri: 7:45–17:00
Sat–Sun: Closed
The clinic operates by appointment. We recommend booking in advance so we can reserve enough time for your pet's care. In urgent situations, call (06) 321 7300 and we'll direct you to the right on-call clinic.

### Booking an appointment

You can book an appointment in two ways:
By phone: Call (06) 321 7300 on weekdays 7:45–17. Our reception staff will help you find a suitable time.
Online booking: Book an appointment around the clock in our online booking system at my.provet.com/elainklinikka-saari. Online booking is fast and easy to use.

### What to bring to your appointment

Please bring any previous medical records or discharge summaries, current medication and your pet's vaccination card to the appointment. If your pet is insured, bring the insurance certificate — we offer direct billing with LähiTapiola, Agria and Pohjola. Cats should be brought in a carrier and dogs on a lead.

### Emergencies

Our clinic does not provide round-the-clock emergency care. In emergencies outside opening hours, call the clinic on (06) 321 7300, where a recorded message will direct you to the nearest on-call clinic. In acute, life-threatening situations, contact an on-call veterinarian immediately.

### Location on the map

# Staff | Saari Animal Clinic

URL: https://elainklinikkasaari.fi/en/staff/
Last updated: 2026-10-25

## Staff

Saari Animal Clinic's care team consists of 14 skilled professionals — experienced veterinarians and veterinary nurses. Our veterinarians have decades of experience in small-animal medicine and further training in areas including orthopedics, cardiology, dentistry and endoscopy. Our veterinary nurses care for patients warmly before, during and after procedures. Meet our team below.

### Veterinarians

#### Leena Sandström

Veterinarian
I qualified as a veterinarian in 1997 and have worked as a small-animal vet for almost my entire career.
I have specialized in heart disease and completed the European ESAVS Certificate in Small Animal Veterinary Practice / Cardiology. I am authorized to perform the Finnish Kennel Club's official cardiac examinations (auscultation, ultrasound and ECG). I have trained in abdominal ultrasound on Finnish courses (Fennovet) and in Europe (ESAVS).
My professional interests focus on heart disease and internal medicine in dogs and cats.
Through careful examination and up-to-date knowledge, I aim to ensure that your pet receives appropriate care.
Areas of expertise: Heart disease, internal medicine, cardiac and abdominal ultrasound

#### Pamela Kvarngård

Veterinarian · Cat Advocate
I have worked as a small-animal veterinarian since 2013, and today my work focuses especially on orthopedic patients. I have pursued further training in areas including orthopedic surgery (AOVET, ESAVS, etc.) and dental disease (Accesia Academy).
It is important to me to stay up to date with new research, treatment methods and techniques — continuous training is an essential part of providing the best possible care.
My core professional interests are orthopedics, soft-tissue surgery and dental care. I find it especially rewarding to help animals regain their comfort, mobility and a good quality of life, and this motivates me in my work every day.
I am the clinic's Cat Advocate within the Cat Friendly Clinic program, making sure our feline patients' visits are as calm and stress-free as possible.

##### Continuing education

- 2026 – Orthopaedics III (shoulder, elbow and carpus, including arthroscopy), ESAVS, Vienna, Austria (5 days)
- 2019 – Orthopaedics II, ESAVS, Cremona, Italy (5 days)
- 2019 – Orthopaedics I, ESAVS, Vienna, Austria (5 days)
Areas of expertise: Orthopedics, soft-tissue surgery, dental care, cat-friendly care

#### Assaf Wydra

Veterinarian
I have worked as a small-animal veterinarian since 2011, and today my work focuses mainly on dental care, endoscopy and the care of wild animals. I have completed further training in veterinary dentistry (Accesia Academy) as well as in endoscopy and wildlife care.
Following and making use of new technology is an essential part of my professional development and helps me provide my patients with the highest possible standard of care.
My professional interests are especially dental care, endoscopy and the practical application of new technological innovations in clinical work. Alongside clinic work, I actively do voluntary pro bono work with wild animals, which I find a very meaningful and important part of my role as a veterinarian.

##### Continuing education

- 2026 – Small Animal Anesthesia and Pain Management, 4-day in-house course with veterinary anesthesiologist Nathalie Swirsky-Zuck (28 CPD points)
- 2024 – Endoscopy of the upper gastrointestinal and respiratory tract: diagnosis and treatment, CPD-Vet, Israel (2 days)
- 2021 – Dentistry II, Accesia Academy, Halmstad, Sweden (5 days)
- 2020 – Critical care, anaesthesia and analgesia of exotic pets, Fennovet (2 days, online)

Areas of expertise: Dental care, endoscopy, wildlife care, technological innovation

#### Nina Haglund

Veterinarian
I have worked as a veterinarian since 2016/2017 and have been part of the Saari Animal Clinic team since 2020. It is important to me to combine a calm and empathetic approach with a way of working that emphasizes patient safety and strong clinical skill — I want both the animals and their owners to feel safe at my appointments.
Before my veterinary career I qualified as a pharmacist, which gives a strong foundation for understanding pharmacology and medication. I have complemented my skills with further training in dental disease (Accesia Academy) and studies in soft-tissue surgery (ESAVS).
My professional interests focus especially on surgery, dental care and dermatology. In my work I am motivated by continuous development — and above all by being able to support animal welfare every day.

##### Continuing education

- 2026 – Feline Medicine: Advanced Clinical Challenges, ESAVS, Palma de Mallorca, Spain (3 days)
Areas of expertise: Surgery, dental care, dermatology

#### Merja Autio

Veterinarian

# Wildlife care | Saari Animal Clinic

URL: https://elainklinikkasaari.fi/en/wildlife/
Last updated: 2026-09-19

Wildlife department

## Small patient, wild life.

We treat injured wild animals in Ostrobothnia — hedgehogs, eagles, swans, bats, squirrels.
In partnership with Nordic Wildlife Care, on a volunteer basis and free of charge.
100% Free of charge
8+ Species / year
36 yrs In Vaasa
Young swan · brought by police · October 2025
What we do

### Emergency care for every wild neighbour.

Saari Animal Clinic works with Nordic Wildlife Care to care for injured
and weakened wild animals. Our volunteer work is free for the clinic —
we believe every wild animal deserves a chance to return to nature.
We provide diagnostics and emergency care: imaging, surgery, pain
management and supportive care. Once stabilised, patients move on to
rehabilitation at Nordic Wildlife Care, and the goal is always to
release them back into the wild.
"Wild patients always hold a special place in our hearts. We wish every
little fighter a quick recovery and many safe adventures back in the wild."
The species we treat range from hedgehogs, bats and squirrels to swans
and white-tailed eagles — and every story reminds us how human activity
touches wild life right outside our doors.
A little bat got warmth and rest — within hours, ready to return to the night sky.
8+ Species treated
100+ Cases / year
0 € To the finder
2011→ Wildlife care

Every year more than a hundred wild patients are brought to our clinic.
Here are eleven stories that moved the most readers on Facebook — all carrying
the same message: a small act can save a wild life.

A young fox arrived in a fox trap, limping on its right hind leg. Sedation and

clinic's heart.

#### A small life, a big reminder — mouse trap

This wild hedgehog's front paw had been caught in a mouse trap. One
toe was completely severed, another dislocated, the whole paw swollen
and infected. For a hedgehog, front paws are vital — without the
ability to dig there is no chance of survival. Traps left outside
are a silent danger to wildlife.

Read the story on Facebook
What threatens our wildlife

### Most threats are homemade.

Most of our wild patients' injuries come from human activity — where the
garden meets the wild. A small change in routine can save a life.

#### Robot lawnmowers

A nocturnal robot and a nocturnal hedgehog don't mix. Run robot mowers
only in daylight — a hedgehog's defence (rolling into a ball) is no
protection against the blades.

#### Traps and poisons

Outdoor mouse traps catch a hedgehog's paw just as easily as a mouse.
Rodenticides end up in the food chain of predators and hedgehogs. Use
poison-free, enclosed alternatives.

#### Plastic strings and nets

Fishing line, bale twine and plastic netting tighten around wildlife.
Cut strings into pieces before disposal and always pack out your
fishing waste.

#### Traffic and construction

Road traffic kills hundreds of thousands of hedgehogs in Europe every
year. Wind power and solid fences create their own problems. Even a
small hedgehog hole in the fence (13×13 cm) helps.
Found an injured wild animal?

### Stay calm — and call us.

Contact the clinic before bringing the animal in, so we can prepare. If
needed, we'll direct you to Nordic Wildlife Care's rehabilitation centre
instead.
Call (06) 321 7300
- Keep your distance — don't chase or pick up with bare hands. Use thick gloves or a towel.
- Place the animal in a cardboard box with air holes and soft cloth at the bottom. Keep the box dark and quiet.
- Do not feed or give water — the wrong food or fluids can kill faster than the original injury.
- Call the clinic and briefly describe the species, location and nature of the injury. You'll get detailed next-step instructions.
Support Nordic Wildlife Care

### Nordic Wildlife Care looks after patients after the clinic.

Our clinic provides emergency care on a volunteer basis, but rehabilitation,
food and release happen through Nordic Wildlife Care. Their work depends on
donations — every euro goes directly to wildlife care.
Donate to Nordic Wildlife Care →
Read more

# Veterinarian Vaasa | Saari Animal Clinic since 1989

URL: https://elainklinikkasaari.fi/en/veterinarian-vaasa/
Last updated: 2026-10-21

## Veterinarian in Vaasa — Saari Animal Clinic

Looking for a veterinarian in Vaasa? Saari Animal Clinic has served the Dragnäsbäck neighbourhood since 1989 — over three generations and tens of thousands of pets cared for. We're a privately owned, independent small-animal clinic: no chain, no corporate playbook. Every treatment decision rests with your veterinarian personally. Our team includes 6 veterinarians and 8 veterinary nurses, and we work in Finnish, Swedish and English.

### Our veterinarians

Here's our team — all experienced veterinarians who keep their skills current through ongoing post-graduate education.
Pamela Kvarngård — Clinic director, veterinarian since 2013. Areas of focus: orthopaedics, soft-tissue surgery and dentistry. Post-graduate training in orthopaedic surgery (AOVET, ESAVS) and dentistry (Accesia Academy). Languages: Swedish, Finnish, English.
Leena Sandström — Veterinarian since 1997, almost her entire career in small-animal medicine. Areas of focus: heart diseases, internal medicine, cardiac and abdominal ultrasound. ESAVS Certificate in Cardiology. Authorised by the Finnish Kennel Club to perform official cardiac examinations (auscultation, ultrasound, ECG). Ultrasound training with Fennovet and ESAVS. Languages: Swedish, Finnish, English.
Assaf Wydra — Veterinarian since 2011. Areas of focus: dentistry, endoscopy, wildlife medicine and the application of new clinical technology. Post-graduate training in dentistry (Accesia Academy) and endoscopy. Active pro bono wildlife rehabilitation work. Languages: English, Finnish, Hebrew.
Nina Haglund — Veterinarian since 2016/2017, with the Saari team since 2020. Areas of focus: surgery, dentistry and dermatology. Her background as a pharmacist provides a solid grounding in pharmacology and pharmacotherapy. Post-graduate training in dentistry (Accesia Academy) and soft-tissue surgery (ESAVS). Languages: Swedish, Finnish, English.
Merja Autio — Veterinarian since 2024, with the Saari team since April 2025. Graduated in summer 2025 from Eesti Maaülikool in Tartu. Areas of focus: soft-tissue surgery and exotic-animal medicine. Languages: Finnish, English.

### What we treat

We care for dogs, cats and small mammals — and exotic species and wildlife as well. Our most common services:
- General check-ups and annual exams — wellness exams, vaccinations, parasite control. Read about vaccinations.
- Dental care — scaling, extractions, treatment of tooth resorption with digital dental X-ray. Dental services.
- Surgery — spays and neuters, soft-tissue surgery, orthopaedic procedures (TTA, lateral suture). Surgical services.
- Cardiac examinations — echocardiography, ECG, blood-pressure monitoring. Official Finnish Kennel Club cardiac examinations. Cardiac diagnostics.
- Ultrasound and X-ray — abdominal and urinary tract imaging, pregnancy ultrasound, digital radiography. Ultrasound.
- Internal medicine — diabetes, hyperthyroidism, kidney disease, IBD and other chronic conditions. Internal medicine.
- Endoscopy — gastroscopy, video otoscopy. Endoscopy.
- Ophthalmology, dermatology, acupuncture, rehabilitation — see our full service list.
We're also an International Cat Care–accredited Cat Friendly Clinic (Silver level) — feline-friendly facilities and handling are built into every consultation.
🐈 Cat vet in Vaasa – read more about our cat care

### Location — a vet near central Vaasa

Our address is Gerbyntie 18, 65230 Vaasa, in the Dragnäsbäck district at the Gerbyntie/Pohjolankatu junction known locally as Pukinkulma — about 5 minutes' drive from central Vaasa. Our clients come from across the Vaasa region:
- Central Vaasa and Palosaari — 5–10 minutes
- Dragnäsbäck and Gerby — under 5 minutes, neighbouring districts
- Sundom, Vähäkyrö, Lillkyro — 15–20 minutes
- Mustasaari (Korsholm), Vöyri (Vörå), Maalahti (Malax) — we serve the Swedish-speaking Ostrobothnian region as well
- Kristinestad, Närpes, Kaskö, Teuva — about an hour's drive; our page for visitors from the south
There's free parking directly in front of the clinic, with space for several cars.
By bus: the nearest stops are on Gerbyntie right outside the clinic, less than 100 m away. Vaasa local route line 1 runs along the way. Check timetables at vaasa.fi/joukkoliikenne.
📍 Open in Google Maps

### Opening hours

Monday–Friday 7:45–17:00. Closed Saturdays, Sundays and Finnish public holidays.
We do not operate an after-hours emergency service. During opening hours we always try to fit urgent cases into the day's schedule — call (06) 321 7300 directly and we'll assess the situation together. Outside opening hours, please contact one of the emergency veterinary services in the Vaasa region.

### Payment and insurance

We accept the major debit/credit cards. We don't accept cash. Direct insurance billing is available with Lähitapiola, Agria and Pohjola — meaning the insurer's share is settled directly at the clinic, so you don't need to pay the full amount up front and claim it back afterwards.

### Frequently asked questions

#### Do you have an emergency service in Vaasa?

We do not operate an after-hours emergency service. During opening hours (Mon–Fri 7:45–17:00) we always try to fit urgent cases into the day — call us directly at (06) 321 7300. Outside opening hours, see our emergency guidance for the Vaasa region and the Northern Finland emergency number 0600 399 299.

#### Do I need an appointment?

Yes, an appointment is recommended so we can examine your pet without rush. Book by phone at (06) 321 7300 or online. Tuesday afternoons 15:30–16:00 we offer drop-in vaccinations without an appointment, at 10 % less than a booked appointment.

#### Do you serve Swedish-speaking clients?

Yes. Pamela Kvarngård, Leena Sandström and Nina Haglund consult in Swedish, and our entire staff is comfortable working in this bilingual region.

#### Do you treat wildlife?

We accept injured wildlife, with hedgehog rehabilitation as a particular focus area led by Assaf Wydra (in cooperation with Siilisaari ry). Please call first: (06) 321 7300.

#### Which pets do you treat?

We treat dogs, cats, rodents, rabbits and other small mammals. We also accept exotic species — Merja Autio has a particular interest in exotic-animal medicine. Please call first at (06) 321 7300 so we can schedule an appointment suited to your animal.

#### I'm a tourist or new to Vaasa — can you still see my pet?

Absolutely. We see visiting pets and new arrivals to Finland regularly. Bring any vaccination records and EU pet passport if you have them. Booking ahead is appreciated; same-day appointments are often available — call us to check.

# Cat Vet in Vaasa – Cat Friendly Clinic | Saari Animal Clinic

URL: https://elainklinikkasaari.fi/en/cat-veterinarian-vaasa/
Last updated: 2026-10-21

## Cat vet in Vaasa – calm, unhurried care for your cat

Saari Animal Clinic is an ISFM Cat Friendly Clinic at Silver level. Cats have their own waiting area away from dogs, their own consulting room and their own hospital ward, and our team is trained to handle them gently. We have looked after cats in the Vaasa region since 1989, from their first kitten vaccinations through to old age, in Finnish, Swedish and English.
First in Ostrobothnia. In 2020 we became the first accredited Cat Friendly Clinic in Ostrobothnia. Yle (in Finnish) and Vasabladet (in Swedish) both wrote about it.
Book online
Call (06) 321 7300

### What a cat-friendly visit looks like here

Own waiting area. Cats wait in their own area, screened from dogs, with raised shelves so the carrier never has to sit on the floor.
A consulting room only for cats. One of our consulting rooms is for cats only. Dogs are never examined there.
No scruffing, no pulling. We never scruff a cat or pull it out of its carrier. We can take the top off the carrier and examine your cat where it feels safe.
Pain relief comes first. A cat that is in pain gets pain relief before the examination, not after.
A ward just for cats. Cats that stay with us for the day are cared for in a cat-only ward, separate from the dog ward, with soft bedding and a place to hide.
Blood pressure in the awake cat. We measure blood pressure with cuffs made for cats. This matters most for older cats and for cats with kidney, thyroid or heart disease.
Calming scent. We use Feliway diffusers in the waiting and reception areas and Feliway spray on examination tables and towels.
Our Cat Advocate. Veterinarian Pamela Kvarngård is the clinic's Cat Advocate. She makes sure the Cat Friendly standards are followed in everyday work.
Read more: A less stressful vet visit for your cat

### If your cat is afraid of the vet

Fear at the vet is normal and does not make a cat “difficult”. Leave the carrier out at home with a familiar blanket inside, so it is not only brought out for vet visits. Cover it with a towel in the car. Tell us when you book if your cat is very frightened, and we will plan the visit around it. For a very anxious cat we can also discuss calming medication to give at home before the visit.

Vaccinations and kittens. Kittens are vaccinated at 12 and 16 weeks, with a booster at 12 months. After that, adult cats are vaccinated every 1–3 years depending on the vaccine. ### When should you bring your cat in?

Cats are good at hiding illness, so even small changes are worth checking. Book an appointment if your cat:
- eats or drinks more or less than usual, or loses weight
- vomits often or has diarrhoea
- urinates more often or outside the litter box
- hides, moves less or no longer jumps up
- has bad breath, drools or chews on one side
- scratches or licks itself much more than usual
These are emergencies: if your cat breathes with its mouth open or struggles to breathe, or if a male cat strains in the litter box and passes little or no urine. During opening hours, call us straight away. Outside opening hours, contact the emergency vet. Emergency guidance for the Vaasa region

# Dog and Cat Teeth Cleaning in Vaasa | Saari Animal Clinic

URL: https://elainklinikkasaari.fi/en/services/dental-care/
Last updated: 2026-09-19

Back to homepage

## Teeth cleaning, extractions and dental care for dogs and cats in Vaasa

Dog teeth cleaning at Saari Animal Clinic in Vaasa costs €303 (under 20 kg) or €353 (over 20 kg); for cats €263. The price includes general anaesthesia, ultrasonic scaling, an oral examination and a dental chart. Dental X-rays (€59–99) are taken at the same time, and you get a cost estimate for any extractions before the procedure.

### Why is dental care important?

Dental disease is among the most common health problems in pets. By the age of three, the majority of dogs and cats have tartar and gingivitis. Untreated dental damage progresses silently — animals instinctively hide pain, so owners often notice the problem only when it has advanced significantly. Regular teeth cleaning and dental care extend your pet's lifespan and significantly improve quality of life.
Periodontal disease in an adult dog: heavy tartar on the premolars and molars, and the gums are inflamed and receding in places. Photo: Saari Animal Clinic.

### Dental care prices

Dental check on an awake pet (assessment) €32
Teeth cleaning (scaling), cat €263
Teeth cleaning (scaling), dog under 20 kg €303
Teeth cleaning (scaling), dog over 20 kg €353
Surcharge, dog over 40 kg €50
Dental X-rays with dental treatment €59–99
Deciduous tooth removal, 1–2 teeth €453
Deciduous tooth removal, 3–4 teeth €533
Permanent tooth extraction estimate after examination
The teeth-cleaning price includes general anaesthesia, ultrasonic scaling, an oral examination and a dental chart. Permanent tooth extractions have no fixed price: it is set after the clinical examination and X-rays and depends on the number of teeth, the number and condition of the roots and the time required. You receive an estimate before the procedure. All prices are in our price list. Direct insurance billing is available for LähiTapiola, Agria and Pohjola customers.

### Teeth cleaning — how is it done?

Tartar is removed with an ultrasonic scaler from the tooth surfaces and from below the gum line, where tartar and bacteria cause gingivitis and periodontitis. The procedure is always done under general anaesthesia: on an awake animal only the visible part of the teeth can be cleaned, the area below the gum line cannot be reached, and the mouth cannot be properly examined or X-rayed. "Anaesthesia-free teeth cleaning" is cosmetic and does not treat the disease itself — which is why we do not offer it. Teeth cleaning with X-rays usually takes about 1–2 hours; any extractions extend the procedure.

### Tooth extractions

A tooth is extracted when it can no longer be saved: in advanced periodontitis, tooth resorption, root infection, or when the tooth is fractured into the pulp. Extractions are done surgically — multi-rooted teeth are sectioned and the roots removed completely. The wound is closed with dissolvable sutures and pain medication is sent home. Extractions are priced case by case based on the clinical examination and X-rays. Deciduous teeth are often removed during spay or neuter surgery under the same anaesthesia.

### Dental X-rays — seeing what is hidden

Dental X-rays are the most important diagnostic tool in dentistry. Over half of dental diseases are invisible on visual examination — root infections, tooth resorption, cysts and bone loss are only revealed on radiographs. At our clinic, all teeth are radiographed with digital dental X-ray as part of every dental treatment (€59–99).
Dental X-ray of a cat under general anaesthesia: an endotracheal tube protects the airway and the X-ray tube is positioned at the mouth. Photo: Saari Animal Clinic.
Dental radiograph of a cat’s left lower jaw: tooth resorption in the mandibular third premolar (307). The tooth was extracted. Image: Saari Animal Clinic.

### How does the procedure work?

Before the procedure, a health check and blood tests are performed as needed. Adult dogs and cats are fasted 8–12 hours before anaesthesia (water until the morning). The procedure is carried out under inhalation anaesthesia with comprehensive pain relief, and during anaesthesia we continuously monitor heart rate, oxygen saturation, blood pressure and temperature. Tartar is removed, dental X-rays are taken, diseased teeth are treated, and damaged teeth are extracted if necessary. Patients are typically discharged the same day. Read more about anaesthesia safety.

### Common dental diseases in dogs and cats

Periodontitis — inflammation of the tooth-supporting tissues — is the most common dental disease and leads to tooth loss and chronic pain when advanced. Tooth resorption is particularly common in cats, where the tooth structure breaks down from within — often invisible on visual examination and very painful. Fractured teeth (especially canines) predispose to root infections. Retained deciduous teeth when permanent teeth erupt cause alignment problems, especially in small dog breeds. Each of these conditions can be diagnosed and treated at our clinic.

### Home dental care — prevention starts at home

Regular tooth brushing is the most effective way to prevent tartar buildup and gingivitis. Start by gently getting your pet used to fingers and a pet-specific toothpaste — human toothpaste is not suitable for animals due to fluoride and xylitol content. Daily brushing is the goal, but 2–3 times per week already produces meaningful results. VOHC-certified chew products and dental diets complement home care. Note, however, that home care does not replace professional teeth cleaning, which can only be performed under anaesthesia.

### Recovery after dental care

Patients are typically discharged the same day and can be collected in the afternoon. Soft food is recommended for 1–3 days, especially if teeth have been extracted. Take-home anti-inflammatory pain medication is provided when needed, along with instructions for use. Most pets return to normal eating and play within 24–48 hours. If teeth have been extracted or gum procedures performed, a follow-up appointment is scheduled for 5 days later to verify healing.

### Frequently asked questions about teeth cleaning and dental care

How much does dog teeth cleaning cost? Dog teeth cleaning (scaling) at Saari Animal Clinic costs €303 (under 20 kg) or €353 (over 20 kg), with a €50 surcharge for dogs over 40 kg. The price includes general anaesthesia, ultrasonic scaling, an oral examination and a dental chart. Dental X-rays are taken with the treatment, €59–99.
How much does cat teeth cleaning cost? Cat teeth cleaning costs €263. The price includes general anaesthesia, scaling, an oral examination and a dental chart. Dental X-rays (€59–99) are taken with the treatment.
How much does a dog or cat tooth extraction cost? Permanent tooth extractions have no fixed price. The price is set after the clinical examination and X-rays and depends on the number of teeth, the number and condition of the roots and the time required. You receive an estimate before the procedure. Deciduous tooth removal costs €453 (1–2 teeth) or €533 (3–4 teeth).
Can a dog's teeth be cleaned without anaesthesia? Not properly. On an awake animal only the visible tooth surface can be cleaned — the area below the gum line, where the disease starts, cannot be reached, and the mouth cannot be examined or X-rayed. Anaesthesia-free cleaning is cosmetic and does not treat the disease. That is why all dental treatments at our clinic are done under general anaesthesia with continuous monitoring of vital signs.
When should a dog have its teeth cleaned? When there is visible tartar, the gums are red or the breath smells bad — gingivitis has then already begun. For dogs and cats over 3 years we recommend a yearly dental check (awake, €32), earlier for small breeds. At the check we assess whether a cleaning is needed and whether any teeth need extracting.
How long does teeth cleaning take? Teeth cleaning with X-rays usually takes about 1–2 hours. Extractions extend the procedure. Your pet is dropped off in the morning and usually collected the same afternoon.
How do I know if my pet needs dental care? Signs of dental disease include bad breath, tartar, red gums, difficulty eating and drooling. We recommend a dental check during the consultation — problems often go unnoticed from the outside.
How does a dog recover from a tooth extraction? Most pets eat and play normally within 24–48 hours. Soft food is recommended for 1–3 days, pain medication is sent home, and dissolvable sutures disappear on their own. A follow-up visit is booked about 5 days later to confirm healing.
Can I brush my pet's teeth at home? Yes, and it is the most effective form of home care. Always use toothpaste designed for pets — fluoride and xylitol in human toothpaste are toxic to animals. Start gently with a finger, then progress to a soft children's toothbrush or a special pet toothbrush. Daily brushing gives the best protection, but 2–3 times a week already helps significantly.
When should retained baby teeth be removed? If the permanent teeth have erupted but the baby tooth is still in place (persistent baby tooth), it can cause dental misalignment and inflammation. They are usually removed during spay or neuter surgery, while the dog is already under anaesthesia — this avoids a separate anaesthesia.

# Dog Heart Ultrasound in Vaasa | Saari Animal Clinic

URL: https://elainklinikkasaari.fi/en/services/cardiac-examinations/
Last updated: 2026-09-19

Back to homepage

## Dog Heart Ultrasound and Cardiac Examinations in Vaasa

### What is a dog heart ultrasound?

A dog heart ultrasound, i.e. an ultrasound examination of the heart (echocardiography), is a painless examination in which the structure and function of the heart are seen in real time. It is the single most important examination for diagnosing heart disease in dogs and cats, assessing its severity and planning medication. At Saari Animal Clinic, heart ultrasounds are performed by veterinarian Leena Sandström, who is approved by the Finnish Kennel Club for official cardiac ultrasound examinations and holds the European ESAVS certificate in cardiology. The examination is performed on an awake dog lying on its side and usually requires no sedation. The heart ultrasound takes about 20–30 minutes, and the results are discussed with the owner immediately afterwards.

### What is examined in a heart ultrasound?

A heart ultrasound measures the size of the heart chambers and atria, wall thickness and the contractility of the heart muscle. Doppler examination shows blood flow through the valves and identifies valve leaks and narrowings. Measurements are indexed to the dog's weight, so the results of a small and a large dog are comparable. A heart ultrasound detects, among others, degenerative mitral valve disease (MMVD), dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), congenital heart defects such as patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) and aortic or pulmonic stenosis, as well as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) in cats. The examination also tells whether the heart is already enlarged to the point where medication should be started.
Heart ultrasound of a 13-year-old dog with mitral valve disease (MMVD, ACVIM stage C): the mitral valve leaflets are thickened and the left atrium is markedly enlarged. Image: Saari Animal Clinic.

### Official heart ultrasound for dogs (Kennel Club)

We perform the Finnish Kennel Club's official cardiac ultrasound examinations for breeding dogs. The official heart ultrasound is carried out by Kennel Club-approved examiner Leena Sandström, and the result is recorded in the Kennel Club database. The official examination includes listening to the heart (auscultation) and the ultrasound examination. Bring the dog's registration certificate; the identification (microchip) is checked before the examination. If your breed's PEVISA programme or breeding recommendation only requires cardiac auscultation, the official auscultation can also be performed by veterinarian Assaf Wydra. Both are on the Kennel Club's list of heart veterinarians.

### Dog heart ultrasound price

Heart ultrasound prices at Saari Animal Clinic: cardiac ultrasound for suspected disease or follow-up 376–476 €, official cardiac ultrasound for a dog 403 € (under 40 kg) or 453 € (over 40 kg), official cardiac auscultation 80 € or 37 € during another visit. A cat heart ultrasound is priced the same as a dog's (376–476 €). Current prices are in our price list. Direct insurance billing is available for LähiTapiola, Agria and Pohjola customers.

### When does a dog need a heart ultrasound?

A heart ultrasound is indicated when the vet hears a murmur, for example at a vaccination visit, when the dog coughs especially at night or at rest, tires faster than before on walks, breathes rapidly at rest (over 30 breaths per minute while asleep) or faints. For at-risk breeds — Cavalier King Charles Spaniel, Dobermann, Boxer, Great Dane, Irish Wolfhound and many small breeds — we recommend the first heart ultrasound before any symptoms appear. A heart ultrasound is also advisable before anaesthesia of a senior dog with a heart murmur, and before breeding.

### How to prepare for a heart ultrasound?

No fasting is needed for a heart ultrasound unless sedation has been agreed separately. Give any heart medication as usual unless the vet instructs otherwise. A small patch of fur is shaved on both sides of the chest so that the ultrasound probe makes good contact with the skin. Bring previous cardiac reports and, for an official examination, the dog's registration certificate. A calm walk before the visit helps the dog relax on the examination table.

### Cat heart ultrasound

The most common heart disease in cats is hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), in which the heart muscle thickens. It often progresses with no symptoms at all, and the first sign may be a sudden blood clot or breathing difficulty. A cat heart ultrasound is indicated if the heart has a murmur or gallop rhythm, the cat breathes rapidly or belongs to an at-risk breed (Maine Coon, Ragdoll, British Shorthair, Sphynx). We also recommend a heart ultrasound before anaesthesia if the cat has a murmur. A cat heart ultrasound is performed awake and takes about 15–20 minutes.

### ECG and Holter monitoring

The heart ultrasound shows the structure of the heart, the ECG its electrical activity. An ECG identifies arrhythmias, and a 24-hour Holter recording at home catches rare rhythm disturbances that do not show on a short ECG. For a dog that faints, Holter monitoring is often the most important complementary examination to the heart ultrasound.

### Most common heart diseases in dogs and cats

In dogs, mitral valve disease (MMVD, myxomatous mitral valve degeneration) is the most common heart condition and affects particularly small breeds such as the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel, Dachshund, and Poodle. Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is typical of large breeds such as the Dobermann, Great Dane, and Boxer. In cats, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is the most common heart disease — it often progresses silently, and the first sign may be a sudden severe problem such as a blood clot or acute heart failure. Every one of these can be detected with a heart ultrasound and treated in time.
Colour Doppler image of the heart of a 13-year-old dog with mitral valve disease (MMVD): the leak through the valve shows as a mosaic jet into the enlarged left atrium. Image: Saari Animal Clinic.
Side-view chest X-ray of a dog with a heart change resembling dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM phenotype): the heart shadow is enlarged. Image: Saari Animal Clinic.

### Medication and follow-up

When heart disease is diagnosed, the right medication and regular follow-up are essential. Pimobendan, ACE inhibitors, diuretics (furosemide, torasemide), and beta blockers are commonly used in treatment. Each pet gets an individual treatment plan based on the type and stage of the heart disease. Follow-up usually includes a repeat heart ultrasound, blood pressure measurement, blood tests (kidney values, electrolytes), and sometimes a chest X-ray. The follow-up interval depends on the stage of the disease — typically around every 12 months once the patient is stable.

### Home care and quality of life

Home care plays an important role in the treatment of heart disease. It is good to monitor resting respiratory rate (normal is below 30 breaths per minute when asleep), exercise tolerance, appetite, and energy levels. Medications must be given consistently at the same times. Exercise should be kept moderate — strenuous activity is to be avoided, but gentle walks are good. A special cardiac diet can support treatment. With proper treatment, many pets with heart disease can live good-quality lives for years after diagnosis.

### Frequently asked questions about dog heart ultrasound

How much does a dog heart ultrasound cost? A cardiac ultrasound for suspected disease or follow-up costs 376–476 €. An official Finnish Kennel Club echocardiogram for a dog costs 403 € (under 40 kg) or 453 € (over 40 kg). Official cardiac auscultation costs 80 €, or 37 € during another visit. Current prices are in our price list.
Does my dog need sedation for a heart ultrasound? Usually not. The heart ultrasound is performed on an awake dog lying on its side, and the examination is painless. Only a very restless dog receives light sedation, which does not affect the results.
How long does a heart ultrasound take? A dog heart ultrasound takes about 20–30 minutes, a cat's about 15–20 minutes. Results are discussed with the owner immediately after the examination, and a written report is provided.
Does Saari Animal Clinic have a Kennel Club-approved echocardiographer? Yes. Veterinarian Leena Sandström is approved by the Finnish Kennel Club for official cardiac ultrasound examinations and performs them at our clinic. Official cardiac auscultation can also be carried out by veterinarian Assaf Wydra. Both are on the Kennel Club's list of heart veterinarians.
How do I know if my dog has heart disease? Typical signs are coughing especially at night or at rest, tiring faster than before on walks, rapid breathing at rest (over 30 breaths per minute while asleep), fainting and a swollen abdomen. Often, however, the first sign is a heart murmur heard by the vet at a vaccination visit, even though the dog has no symptoms at all.
What is the difference between a heart ultrasound and an ECG? A heart ultrasound (echocardiography) shows the heart's structure, valve function and blood flow in real time — it is the primary examination for diagnosing heart disease. An ECG measures the heart's electrical activity and identifies arrhythmias. The examinations complement each other: ultrasound reveals structural changes, ECG rhythm problems.
How often should the heart ultrasound be repeated? For at-risk breeds we recommend the first heart ultrasound at 1–2 years of age and annually thereafter. For breeding dogs the interval is set by the breed's PEVISA programme or breeding recommendation. If the dog has been diagnosed with heart disease, the follow-up interval is agreed individually, usually every 3–12 months.
Does heart medication need to be given for life? Yes, heart-disease medication is usually lifelong. The role of the medication is to slow disease progression, ease symptoms and improve quality of life — it does not cure the disease itself. Suddenly stopping medication can lead to rapid deterioration.

# Veterinary Surgery in Vaasa | Saari Animal Clinic

URL: https://elainklinikkasaari.fi/en/services/surgery/
Last updated: 2026-10-31

Back to homepage

## Surgery

### Soft tissue surgery

Our clinic performs a wide range of soft tissue surgical procedures: spays and neutering, caesarean sections, tumour removals, foreign body surgery (from stomach or intestines), urinary stone surgery, splenectomies, and eye and ear operations. Each procedure is individually planned according to the patient's needs.

### Orthopaedic surgery

Cruciate ligament repair is the most common orthopaedic procedure in dogs. We use two methods: the lateral suture, which stabilises the knee with strong synthetic material placed outside the joint and suits cats and small dogs, and often medium-sized dogs and older, calmer large dogs as well; and TTA (tibial tuberosity advancement), which permanently changes the forces acting on the knee and suits active dogs and large dogs. We also perform fracture repairs, amputations and femoral head resections.

### Safe anaesthesia

Anaesthesia safety is close to our hearts. For most operations we use inhalation anaesthesia, with continuous monitoring: heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, capnography, ECG and temperature. The clinic has two ventilators and uses a modern balanced anaesthesia protocol. In larger operations, such as dog spays and orthopaedic surgery, a pain-relief infusion (CRI) keeps pain relief steady during surgery and, when needed, afterwards.

### Pre-operative assessment

Safe surgery starts with a thorough patient assessment. Before the operation, we perform a general examination, take the necessary blood tests (haematology, biochemistry), check liver and kidney function, and in older or high-risk patients also cardiac status and blood pressure. Based on these findings, we design an individual anaesthesia protocol and minimise the risks. For high-risk patients, such as brachycephalic breeds or animals with heart disease, we tailor specific protocols.

### Post-operative care and recovery

Recovery begins already in the operating theatre. The patient is actively warmed and pain relief is managed multimodally: opioids, anti-inflammatories, and local anaesthetics together. In recovery, the patient is monitored until fully awake and stable. You will go home with clear instructions on pain relief, exercise restrictions, diet, and wound care. Most patients are discharged the same day. Stitches are removed after 10–14 days.

### Pain management and welfare

Pain has no place in post-operative recovery. We use multimodal pain management, combining different drug groups. This allows more effective pain relief with lower doses and reduces side effects. Adequate pain relief speeds up recovery, reduces stress, and lowers the risk of complications — it is both an animal welfare and a medical priority for us.

### Frequently asked questions about surgery

Is veterinary surgery safe? Yes. We use inhalation anaesthesia for most operations, with comprehensive monitoring (heart, oxygen, blood pressure, temperature). The animal is monitored continuously throughout anaesthesia, and pain relief is always part of the care.
How much does a dog spay cost? Female dog spay starts from €483 and male dog neuter from €383. The price depends on the dog's size. It includes anaesthesia, the surgery, medications and stitch removal.
How long is recovery from surgery? After a spay, recovery usually takes 10–14 days, and after a castration about 7–10 days. After cruciate ligament surgery, exercise is strictly restricted for the first 6–8 weeks, and most dogs are back to normal exercise in about 3–4 months. Home-care instructions are always provided.
Does my pet need to fast before surgery? Yes. Adult dogs and cats are usually fasted for 8–12 hours before surgery (last meal the previous evening). Water is generally allowed until morning. Rabbits are not fasted. You always get instructions when you book.
What's the difference between TTA and lateral suture in cruciate ligament surgery? Lateral suture stabilises the knee with strong synthetic material placed outside the joint. It suits cats and small dogs, and often also medium-sized dogs and older, calmer large dogs. TTA permanently changes the forces on the knee by moving the tibial tuberosity forward with a plate and screws. It suits active and large dogs. We always assess individually which method suits your dog best.
Does the pet need to wear a cone after surgery? Yes – protecting the surgical wound is important. By licking, the pet can open the stitches or cause a wound infection. The traditional plastic Elizabethan collar or softer alternatives like a recovery suit or inflatable collar are good options. We recommend continuous use for 10–14 days, until stitch removal. Pets usually adjust to the protection within 1–2 days.

### Book a consultation

If your pet needs a surgical evaluation, book a consultation appointment. We examine the patient, assess the need for procedures, and plan the best treatment approach together with the owner. Treatments are given at the same clinic by familiar veterinarians — your pet does not need to travel elsewhere.

# Endoscopy for Dogs and Cats in Vaasa | Saari Animal Clinic

URL: https://elainklinikkasaari.fi/en/services/endoscopy/
Last updated: 2026-10-15

Back to homepage

## Endoscopy

### What is endoscopy?

Endoscopy involves minimally invasive examination methods where a thin camera scope is inserted through the body's natural openings to examine internal organs. The method enables precise diagnostics without open surgery, and often treatment at the same time — for example, removal of foreign bodies from the stomach.

### Gastroscopy

Gastroscopy examines and treats digestive tract problems. The most common indication is foreign body removal — endoscopy can often remove socks, toys, and bone fragments without abdominal surgery. Biopsies are also taken for the diagnosis of chronic intestinal diseases (IBD, lymphoma).

### Video otoscopy and ear flushing

Ear examination with magnified video imaging. Visibility into the ear canal is many times greater compared to a traditional otoscope. It enables thorough cleaning and flushing of the ear canal under visual control. Particularly valuable in the investigation and treatment of chronic and recurrent ear infections. Read more: Ear flushing under anesthesia.

### Other endoscopies

Rhinoscopy (nasal cavity endoscopy) for foreign bodies, tumours, and chronic nasal discharge. Cystoscopy (urinary tract endoscopy) for investigating bladder problems. Bronchoscopy (airway endoscopy) for diagnosing chronic cough and respiratory symptoms.

### Frequently asked questions about endoscopy

Is endoscopy painful? Endoscopic examinations are performed under general anaesthesia, so your pet feels no pain during the procedure. After the procedure, the patient may experience mild stomach discomfort, but recovery is usually quick — most patients are discharged the same day. How quickly are results available? Findings and images taken during endoscopy are assessed immediately after the procedure. If biopsy samples are sent to a pathologist, results are usually available within 5–10 working days. The veterinarian reviews the results with the owner and prepares a treatment plan.

# Dog and Cat Vaccinations in Vaasa | Saari Animal Clinic

URL: https://elainklinikkasaari.fi/en/services/vaccinations/
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Back to homepage

## Dog and Cat Vaccinations in Vaasa

### Why is vaccination important?

Vaccination is the most important form of preventive healthcare for pets. Vaccinations protect against serious diseases that can be life-threatening or even fatal. In Finland, the vaccination programme for dogs and cats is based on recommendations from the Finnish Veterinary Association.

### Vaccination prices

Cat RCP vaccine (3-in-1) €75
Cat RCP + rabies €86
Dog DHPPI vaccine (4-in-1) €77
Dog DHPPI + rabies €85
Kennel cough PI €75
Kennel cough KC €77
Dog leptospirosis vaccine €77
Prices are total amounts. See all prices in our price list. Direct insurance billing is available for LähiTapiola, Agria and Pohjola customers.

### Dog vaccinations

Puppies receive their first vaccination at 12 weeks of age, with a booster at 16 weeks. The core vaccination includes protection against distemper, parvovirus, and hepatitis. Rabies vaccination is given from 12 weeks of age. Kennel cough vaccination is recommended for dogs that have frequent contact with other dogs. Adult dogs receive booster vaccinations every 1–3 years.

### Cat and kitten vaccinations

Kitten vaccination: the first vaccine is given at 12 weeks of age and the booster at 16 weeks. The cat RCP vaccine (3-in-1) protects against feline panleukopenia, herpesvirus and calicivirus. Rabies vaccination is given from 12 weeks of age; it is mandatory for cats travelling abroad and recommended for outdoor cats. The first-year booster is given at 12 months, after which an adult cat is vaccinated every 1–3 years depending on the vaccine and lifestyle — indoor cats need the core vaccinations too. If a cat's vaccination is overdue it can usually be given as a single booster; the vet assesses whether two doses are needed when several years have passed since the last vaccination.

### Drop-in vaccinations and travel documents

Our clinic offers drop-in vaccinations without an appointment on Tuesdays from 15:30 to 16:00, at 10 % less than a booked appointment: for example €67.50 for a cat RCP vaccine and €69.30 for a dog DHPPI vaccine. All drop-in prices are in our price list. We also issue EU pet passports and travel documents for pets travelling abroad. Travel document requirements vary by destination country — please contact us well in advance of your trip.

### Puppy vaccination schedule step by step

The puppy's first vaccination series is crucial, as maternal antibody protection wanes at 8–12 weeks of age. A puppy is vaccinated at 12 weeks (distemper, parvovirus, hepatitis) and a booster is given at 16 weeks together with the rabies vaccine. A kitten is vaccinated at 12 weeks (feline panleukopenia, herpes, calici) and a booster at 16 weeks. The first-year booster is given at 12 months — an important milestone where long-lasting immunity is established. After that, vaccination intervals move to every 1–3 years.

### Travelling with your pet

A pet passport is mandatory for all dogs, cats, and ferrets travelling within the EU. Before travelling, your pet needs: a microchip for identification, a valid rabies vaccination (at least 21 days after the first vaccination) and, for dogs, a tapeworm (echinococcus) treatment 1–5 days before returning to Finland (or under the Finnish Food Authority's 28-day rule); no treatment is needed when travelling directly from Finland to Norway or Great Britain. Travelling outside the EU can involve much stricter requirements — a rabies antibody test and quarantine may be required. Start planning your trip at least 4–6 months in advance. We are happy to help with travel documentation. Requirements change from time to time – check the current rules on the Finnish Food Authority website and read more on our EU pet passport page (verified 29 August 2026).

### Vaccine safety and side effects

Vaccinations are among the safest procedures in veterinary medicine, but like all medical interventions they can occasionally cause mild reactions. Common and harmless side effects include mild lethargy, reduced appetite, or slight swelling at the injection site for 1–2 days. Serious reactions such as strong allergic responses (facial swelling, vomiting, weakness) are extremely rare but require immediate veterinary care. We recommend observing your pet for 30 minutes after the vaccination at the clinic and for the rest of the day at home. The benefits of vaccination far outweigh the small risks — unvaccinated pets are at risk of serious, often life-threatening diseases.

### Frequently asked questions about vaccinations

How much does a dog vaccination cost? The dog DHPPI vaccine (4-in-1) costs €77 and with rabies €85; at the Tuesday drop-in it is €69.30, or €76.50 with rabies. Kennel cough vaccine costs €75–77. Prices are total amounts and are listed in our price list.
How much does a cat vaccination cost? The cat RCP vaccine (3-in-1) costs €75 and with rabies €86; at the Tuesday drop-in it is €67.50, or €77.40 with rabies. A kitten's vaccination series is two visits (at 12 and 16 weeks), i.e. €150 in total without rabies.
What vaccinations does a cat need? Every cat, indoor cats included, needs the RCP core vaccine (3-in-1). It protects against feline panleukopenia (cat distemper), feline herpesvirus and calicivirus. A kitten gets it at 12 and 16 weeks, then a booster at 12 months, and after that every 1–3 years depending on the vaccine and the cat's lifestyle. Rabies vaccination can be given from 12 weeks of age. It is recommended for outdoor cats and required for travel abroad. The RCP vaccine costs €75, or €86 with rabies.
At what age is a kitten vaccinated? A kitten's first vaccination is given at 12 weeks of age and the booster at 16 weeks. Rabies vaccine can be given from 12 weeks of age. The first-year booster is given at 12 months.
What if my dog's or cat's vaccination is overdue? An overdue booster can usually be given as a single vaccination. If several years have passed since the last vaccination, the vet assesses whether two doses 3–4 weeks apart are needed. You can also walk in without an appointment on Tuesdays 15:30–16:00.
How often are vaccinations renewed? After the primary series a booster is given one year later. After that, the basic vaccinations for adult dogs and cats are renewed every 1–3 years depending on the vaccine. The rabies vaccine is renewed every 3 years.
Can I come without an appointment? Yes! Bring your pet in for vaccination on Tuesdays between 15:30 and 16:00, no appointment needed. Drop-in vaccinations are 10 % cheaper than a booked appointment. At other times, book by phone on (06) 321 7300 or online.
When can a puppy start the vaccination series? A puppy's first vaccination is given at 12 weeks and the booster at 16 weeks. Before 12 weeks, puppies are protected by maternal antibodies. If a puppy has been imported from abroad or comes from a particularly high-risk environment, vaccination can sometimes start earlier (at 8 weeks) — this is discussed with the veterinarian individually.
Can a pet have side effects from vaccination? Mild side effects are common and harmless: tiredness, reduced appetite or slight swelling at the injection site for 1–2 days. Strong reactions (facial swelling, vomiting, weakness) are very rare but require immediate veterinary care. We recommend monitoring the pet for 30 minutes at the clinic after vaccination, and the rest of the day at home.
What vaccinations are needed for travel? When travelling within EU countries, you need a pet passport, a valid rabies vaccination (at least 21 days from the first vaccination) and a microchip for identification. Dogs additionally need a tapeworm treatment 1–5 days before returning to Finland or under the 28-day rule; no treatment is needed when travelling directly from Finland to Norway or Great Britain. For travel outside the EU, requirements are often stricter — start preparations at least 4–6 months before the trip.

# Ultrasound for Dogs and Cats in Vaasa | Saari Animal Clinic

URL: https://elainklinikkasaari.fi/en/services/ultrasound/
Last updated: 2026-10-15

Back to homepage

## Ultrasound Examinations

### Ultrasound as a diagnostic cornerstone

Ultrasound is one of veterinary medicine's most important imaging methods. It is painless, non-invasive, and does not expose the patient to radiation. The examination is usually performed on an awake patient — only a few require light sedation.

### Abdominal ultrasound

Abdominal ultrasound examines the structure of internal organs and any changes: liver, spleen, kidneys, adrenal glands, bladder, stomach, intestines, pancreas, and lymph nodes. Common indications include vomiting, diarrhoea, weight loss, urination problems, suspected tumours, and general decline. Ultrasound-guided sampling allows biopsies to be taken directly from abnormal tissue.

### Cardiac ultrasound

Cardiac ultrasound (echocardiography) is the primary examination method for heart disease, and at our clinic it is performed by Kennel Club-approved examiner Leena Sandström. Read more about the examination, official Kennel Club echocardiograms and prices on the page Dog Heart Ultrasound and Cardiac Examinations.

### Pregnancy scanning

Ultrasound can confirm pregnancy from approximately day 24 of gestation. The examination assesses fetal viability and development. Radiography can more accurately estimate the number of puppies from day 50 of gestation.

### Frequently asked questions about ultrasound

Is sedation needed for ultrasound? The majority of ultrasound examinations are performed on an awake patient without sedation. The examination is painless — the only preparation is shaving the examination area and applying ultrasound gel to the skin. Particularly restless or anxious patients may receive light sedation. How long does an ultrasound examination take? An abdominal ultrasound typically takes 20–40 minutes depending on findings and the scope of the examination. Cardiac ultrasound takes approximately 15–30 minutes. Pregnancy scanning is the quickest and usually takes 10–15 minutes. Results are communicated to the owner immediately after the examination.

# Skin, Allergy and Ear Care in Vaasa | Saari Animal Clinic

URL: https://elainklinikkasaari.fi/en/services/dermatology/
Last updated: 2026-10-15

Back to homepage

## Skin Diseases, Allergies and Ear Infections

### The most common skin problems

Skin diseases are one of the most common reasons for veterinary visits. One in ten Finnish dogs has allergies, which often manifest as skin infections and ear infections. Typical symptoms include paw licking, ear scratching, face rubbing, redness on the belly, and recurrent ear infections.

### Allergy investigation

When allergy is suspected, food allergens are first ruled out with an elimination diet. If food allergy is excluded, atopic dermatitis (environmental allergy) may be the cause. Allergy blood tests can be taken to identify allergens if needed. Skin and ear samples are examined in the clinic's own laboratory.

### Ear infections

A dog ear infection is one of the most common reasons for a visit: head shaking, ear scratching, bad smell and discharge. At the appointment the ear is examined with an otoscope and a sample of the discharge is checked under the microscope so that treatment hits the right target — yeast, bacteria or ear mites. Recurrent ear infections are most often linked to an underlying allergy, which we work up. For chronic and blocked ears we offer video-otoscopy and ear flushing under anaesthesia (€449–489). Read more: Ear Infections in Dogs — Symptoms, Causes, Treatment and Cost.

### Treatment options

Treatment of skin diseases is individually tailored. Treatment may include elimination diets, allergen-specific immunotherapy (desensitisation), topical treatments, medication, and dietary changes. The goal is to find the cause, not just relieve symptoms.

### Frequently asked questions about skin diseases

Can allergies be cured? Allergy is a chronic condition that usually cannot be completely cured. However, with good management, symptoms can be controlled and your pet's quality of life maintained. Allergen-specific immunotherapy (desensitisation) can significantly reduce the severity of allergies — up to 60–70% of patients benefit from the treatment. The treatment is long-term but can permanently reduce the need for medication. How quickly do treatment results appear? Treatment response for skin diseases depends on the diagnosis. Bacterial skin infections typically respond to antibiotic treatment within 2–4 weeks. An elimination diet requires 6–8 weeks of strict adherence before results can be assessed. Immunotherapy is the slowest — initial results often appear only after 6–12 months.
